homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field; its negative tag 'initiative, explorer and collection are distinct records' (PE-18) keeps the Initiative, its Explorer and its Collection apart as records, while its sibling relation calls the explorer's MMRS record 'the same entity' (PE-19); both are carried. No card is a homonym. 'DPI', the Initiative's own short form (B1, B7; #725), is in the archive also #261's distinction preservation index (a metric of the specification, §6.4) and is not an alias. The general concept 'data provenance' (the field's defined term, F30; W3C PROV in #725) is a sense of the term, not of the entity.
distinct_entities: the Data Provenance Explorer (the Initiative's explorer; its own /non row, datasets/negative-of-the-negative/v2/rows/data-provenance-explorer.json, from the MMRS meta-aggregator: a neighbour, a distinct record, not edited)
Data-Provenance-Collection (the Initiative's GitHub repository and the audit's collection)
Open Model Evolution, the Web Consent Explorer and the AI Observatory (the Initiative's other measurement systems)
MIT Media Lab and MIT Connection Science (institutions of some members; not the operator)
C2PA / Content Credentials, EU AI Act provisions and W3C PROV (the other provenance frameworks #725 sets beside it)

neighbours.relation: the Initiative's explorer, formalized by the MMRS meta-aggregator; the census's sibling record (PE-19) and one of the three names the census gives as aka (PE-01); kept a distinct row (PE-18)

captures.description: THE DATA PROVENANCE INITIATIVE, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a multi-institutional research project—led in part by researchers from MIT—that audits the datasets, licenses, and web domains used to train artificial intelligence models.' Four platforms (the Data Provenance Explorer over 1,800+ datasets, a Web Consent Explorer, Open Model Evolution, an AI Observatory) and three findings (license omission over 70% and error over 50% on hosting platforms, closed datasets concentrated in creative tasks and lower-resource languages, a rise of non-commercial licences driven by synthetic data). Four cards: the initiative's home page ('4,000+ audited datasets; 14,000 tracked web domains'), the arXiv paper, MIT Sloan, Nature Machine Intelligence (1,858 datasets across 44 collections).
